verdicts.reasoning: The raw concern is real in isolation (math.Pow/Ceil is not bit-identical across Go ports) but I could not produce any divergence that reaches consensus. I ran ledger.GroupParameters verbatim on amd64 vs GOARCH=386 over every (participants 1..20000, maxPeers 0..64) pair (1.3M cases): ZERO differences in (groupSize, dimension), even though raw math.Pow(n,1/e) differs on 25 perfect-power inputs in that range. The divergent Pow results do not straddle the integer boundaries GroupParameters' Ceil keys on for realistic sizes, and TimingConsistent carries a 250ms-per-hop margin, so a split requires a governed StepTimeoutMs sitting exactly on the boundary between two dimensions AND a heterogeneous-arch validator set.
verdicts.reproduction: Built a verbatim copy of GroupParameters; `go run` vs `GOARCH=386 go run` over n<=20000, maxPeers 0..64 -> diff count 0. Raw Pow/Ceil comparison -> 25 differing perfect powers, none crossing a dimension boundary. arm64/wasm not tested (no emulator available).
verdicts.realistic_preconditions: Validators on two architectures whose math.Pow differs, AND a 2/3-ratified timing profile whose StepTimeoutMs lands between the two architectures' dimension thresholds. Not demonstrated to exist.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Compute groupSize/dimension with an integer k-th root (binary search) so the result is architecture-independent. Does not change any digest (dimension is not committed, only derived).
verdicts.fix_pitfalls: The integer root must reproduce today's GroupParameters outputs where they are already correct, or the gossip fan-out and TimingConsistent threshold shift for every network at once.
verdicts.interactions: Shares GroupParameters with the peer-DNS topology (NEW-3); an integer-root rewrite touches both the timing check and Neighbors.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified by reading httptransport.go:285-296: handleResolve returns {name,publicKey,address,description, Height: snap.Height, StateDigest: hex(snap.Decided)} with NO commit certificate and NO inclusion proof — the 32-byte digest is an unverified node assertion. The documented cross-check (ResolveRecord comment :257, operating-a-network.md:198: 'query K nodes and compare digests') is weaker than claimed: one dishonest node returns a fabricated address alongside the honest digest string it copied, and a client comparing only digests is fooled. The sound check is to compare the key/address FIELDS (which honest nodes agree on because Address is in StateDigest after fix #4). Also Height=snap.Height is the in-progress height (committed+1) while snap.Decided finalizes committed height snap.Height-1 — an off-by-one in the reported field. Impact is address/display integrity; pay-by-name resolves on-chain at apply time (ui/wallet.go), so funds are not redirected.
verdicts.reproduction: Read httptransport.go:270-300 (no certificate served; Height=snap.Height, digest=hex(snap.Decided)) and node.go Snapshot (Height=n.height is committed+1, Decided=lastDecision is the prior commit). Mechanism evident; no failing test needed for a docs/field bug.
verdicts.realistic_preconditions: One dishonest reference node and a client that trusts digest-equality across nodes as the docs instruct.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Either serve the Commit certificate (and ideally an inclusion proof) with the resolve answer so a client verifies the record against a 2/3 quorum, or correct the docs to say clients must compare the actual publicKey/address fields. Separately, report the committed height snap.Height-1 (or rename the field).
verdicts.fix_pitfalls: Serving a certificate adds a verification path a light client must implement correctly; the field-comparison doc fix is cheap but must be consistent across README/operating-a-network/security docs.
verdicts.interactions: Same digest-scope confusion as C30; the resolve stateDigest is exactly what a user would (wrongly) copy into a PrevStateDigest pin.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced and benign, as round 1 stated. Two conflicting same-key AccountUpdates both apply in block order (account_update.go:83-114, last-wins) with no equivocation detection; a validator may sign parameter-vote and reassignment-vote approvals for competing proposals at one sequence with no flag. These are harmless today: account-update last-wins is deterministic and same-key-only, and quorum intersection + single-use GovernanceSequence stop two conflicting governance actions both enacting. The owner's 'two signings = burn' principle is simply not applied here. Confirmed the declared domains validator-message (DomainValidatorMsg) and server-auth (DomainServerAuth) have no production Sign/Verify caller (only signing_test.go references DomainServerAuth).
verdicts.reproduction: Ran .../scratchpad/burn-rule/ledger/burnrule_poc_test.go::TestPoCConflictingAccountUpdatesBothApply -> FAIL (both conflicting same-key updates applied, last wins, no detection). grep confirmed the two domains are unused in non-test code.
verdicts.realistic_preconditions: One validator double-signing non-vote statements. No concrete harm under current guards.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Optional accountability only: record conflicting same-key governance/account-update signings for the same slot if a social-punishment trail is wanted. Remove or document the unused validator-message/server-auth domains so they are not assumed protected.
verdicts.fix_pitfalls: Adding burn for these would be safe only if the detection is as unforgeable as consensus Evidence (both signatures required); a naive 'two updates seen' check could frame an honest key whose update was duplicated in gossip.
verdicts.interactions: Directly relevant to the owner's 'two signings burns the key' principle: it documents the principle's current scope (consensus votes only). Any future weakening of the quorum/sequence/determinism guards turns these benign cases live.

verdicts.reasoning: Architectural observation, verified. There is no equivocation/burn concept for payments: two different payments from one payer for the same BlockID either both apply (if funds cover) or trip the overdraw ban (ledger.go:160-181) — never recorded as a double-sign, never yielding durable evidence, never burning the key. admitPayment (node.go:432) refuses a second same-block payment only when it would overdraw (a refusal, not a burn). So 'two signings = burn' does not cover the statement that moves money, and a leaked/cracked key drains an account with ONE signing — no second conflicting signing ever arises. Accurate answer to the owner's eMudhra hypothesis: the rule is vote-only and gives no leaked-key fund protection.
verdicts.reproduction: Traced ledger.go:160-181 (overdraw ban, no evidence emitted) and node.go:432-462 (admitPayment refuses, never burns). The end-state harm (drain + same-block name capture) is the C02/NAME-1 PoC. No separate test needed for an absence-of-mechanism claim.
verdicts.realistic_preconditions: Holder of one stolen/cracked ordinary key. Single signing suffices to drain.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Set expectations in docs: the burn rule is consensus-vote-only. For leaked-key fund resilience add out-of-band mechanisms (rotation/revocation, social recovery, or a hold/challenge window on large or name-changing transfers).
verdicts.fix_pitfalls: A 'two conflicting payments burns the key' rule would collide with the overdraw ban (which already destroys the victim's balance) and could be weaponised by a griefer who replays a victim's own payment — see NEW-1.
verdicts.interactions: Tightly coupled to C36 (no rotation) and the owner's recovery model: the only lever against a leaked key is a 2/3 reassignment, which races the thief (C36).

verdicts.reasoning: Verified. Account identity IS the public key; applyAccountUpdates (account_update.go:83-114) only lets an account claim a free name or edit its own attributes — there is no primitive to move a name/stake/seat/address to a NEW key. reassignment.go is the only balance-moving governance action, and it SETS a balance (claw-back), it does not FREEZE. I grepped the whole non-test tree: there is no freeze/hold primitive at all. So the owner's stated recovery model — banks vote 2/3 to FREEZE the key/account/name, then after police a 2/3 vote reassigns — is only half-implementable: the reassignment (claw-back) exists, but the FREEZE that is supposed to stop the thief spending during vote collection does not. The attacker just signs a payment that clears in a near-future block on the vote-collection timescale and typically wins the race. No rotation means a known-weak key cannot be retired either.
verdicts.reproduction: grep for freeze/frozen in non-test code -> only partition-liveness comments, no primitive. Read account_update.go (no owner->successor transfer) and reassignment.go (set-balance only). Recovery-race is an absence-of-primitive observation; no single failing assertion.
verdicts.realistic_preconditions: Any leaked/known-weak ordinary or validator key. The recovery race is the normal case the owner's model is meant to handle.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Add a signed key-rotation/account-transfer primitive (owner signs over a successor key; name, delegation, seat and address move atomically) AND a 2/3 freeze primitive (a governance action that marks a key non-spending without moving its balance) so the documented freeze-then-reassign flow actually stops the thief during vote collection.
verdicts.fix_pitfalls: A freeze flag must be in committed state and under the digest, and must be re-checked in ProcessPayments/admitPayment or it is cosmetic. Rotation must atomically carry the validator seat or a mid-rotation set-change can fork the per-height validator set. A frozen key must still be slashable/reassignable.
verdicts.interactions: This is the load-bearing gap for the owner's whole recovery model (banks freeze then reassign): without a freeze primitive the model's liveness assumption fails. Combines with C35 (single-signing drain) and C02/NAME-1 (name capture) into the full leaked-key outcome.

new_findings.title: Block.Height is attacker-chosen and never tied to the consensus height, so one Byzantine proposer (<1/3) replays old payments / updates / slash-evidence into a current block
locations: ledger/block.go:176-240 (ApplyBlock uses block.Height for every BlockID/evidence-window check, never compares it to the decided height)
ledger/ledger.go:116-128 (LedgerState.Digest omits height — two different consensus heights with the same accounts/params/sequence share a StateDigest)
node/node.go:494-517 (onProposal checks ProposalMsg.Height==n.height but never p.Block.Height)
node/node.go:627-635 (commit re-applies the stored block with no block.Height==height check)
findings.md:356-365 (deferred #7: claims the node layer guards this and it is 'not currently exploitable')
new_findings.description: The replay guard for payments and account-updates is BlockID==block.Height, and the evidence-age window is height-block.Height; all of these use block.Height, a field of the unsigned block body. Nothing — not onProposal, not the driver (it works on digests), not ApplyBlock — ever checks that block.Height equals the height being decided. LedgerState.Digest does not fold in height, so a block built on the current committed state but labelled with an OLD height has a fresh, valid StateDigest and a matching PrevStateDigest. A validator that is the scheduled round-0 proposer (1 of N; in a 4-set that is 25% < the 1/3 BFT bound and recurs constantly) proposes such a block; all honest nodes validate it (signature over the ProposalMsg.Height is correct, ApplyBlock passes because every guard reads the attacker's block.Height), prevote, precommit and commit it. findings.md deferred this (#7) as 'not currently exploitable (the node enforces monotonic height)', but the node enforces monotonicity only on its own n.height counter — it never binds block.Height — so the dismissal is wrong.
new_findings.failure_scenario: 3 honest validators + 1 Byzantine validator key (below 1/3). Honest payment alice->mallory 30 commits at height 1 (alice: 100->70). At a later height H where the Byzantine key is the round-0 proposer, it re-proposes a block built on the current state but with Block.Height=1 carrying the SAME signed payment (BlockID 1). All 3 honest nodes commit it; alice is debited another 30 (70->40). Variants (ledger PoC): re-including a payment whose amount now exceeds the balance trips the overdraw ban and DESTROYS the victim's whole remaining balance and removes the account+name; an old reversed AccountUpdate (re-delegation / name / peer-DNS address) is re-applied; 4997-block-old slash evidence is re-applied by labelling the block height 3, confiscating a recreated account. Breaks security.md's 'a payment applies at most once' and the #5 evidence-age window.
new_findings.attacker: A single Byzantine validator (holds one validator key, must be the scheduled proposer for some round — frequent and within the documented 'single dishonest/compromised validator' threat, below 1/3 power).
new_findings.poc: .../scratchpad/verify-critic/node/poc_critic_height_test.go::TestPoCCriticByzantineProposerReplaysOldPaymentViaBlockHeight -> FAIL through the real 3-honest-node consensus path (alice 70->40, all nodes agree). Four ledger-level variants in .../scratchpad/verify-critic/ledger/poc_critic_height_test.go (ReplayTripsOverdrawBan, FuturePaymentAppliesTwice, StaleEvidenceWindowBypass, OldAccountUpdateReplay) all FAIL.
new_findings.fix: Bind the height into committed state: add Height to LedgerState and its Digest, and have ApplyBlock require block.Height == previousState.Height+1. That closes this, the two certificate-replay findings, and the evidence-window bypass in one move (findings.md already names this as the deferred fix). Interim node-only guard: in onProposal and commit reject any block whose Block.Height != n.height.

new_findings.title: Incremental on-chain address publication (the documented peer-DNS rollout) asymmetrically cuts the gossip graph and permanently halts consensus with all validators honest
locations: node/peerdns.go:25-46 (resolvedPeerAddresses resolves neighbours ONLY among validators that have published an address)
node/peerdns.go:11-20 (resolvePeersFromState calls SetPeers only when resolvedPeerAddresses is non-nil)
node/topology.go:76-116 (Neighbors returns nil when self is not in the key list)
docs/operating-a-network.md:52 and README.md:97-98 (document publishing addresses 'in genesis or via an update' as equivalent)
new_findings.description: When a proper non-empty subset of validators has published an on-chain address, resolvedPeerAddresses on a publisher returns Neighbors over only the address-holders, so each publisher's transport is SetPeers() to just the other publishers — it stops gossiping to the non-publishers. A non-publisher's resolvedPeerAddresses returns nil (its own key is not among the address-holders, so Neighbors returns nil), so it keeps its static all-to-all peers and still broadcasts to everyone, but never hears back from the publishers. The graph is now asymmetric: publishers {0,2} talk only to each other; non-publishers {1,3} broadcast to all but receive nothing from {0,2}. No node ever assembles a 3-of-4 quorum whose precommits also propagate — {0,2} get prevote-quorum but their precommits reach only each other; {1,3} never reach prevote-quorum — so no block ever commits. Because publishing the remaining addresses needs a committed block, there is no recovery and no checkpoint to catch up to. This is reachable by following the documented 'publish via an update' rollout, or by a genesis where only some validators carry an address.
new_findings.failure_scenario: 4 equal honest validators. Two of them submit the documented AccountUpdate publishing their gossip address (bound to block 2). Blocks 1-2 commit (both addresses land in committed state on all nodes). From height 3 the gossip graph is cut as above and the network stops: PoC shows heights [3,3,3,3] after 6s versus the control (no publication) racing to height 76. No attacker; no node recovers.
new_findings.attacker: None — triggered by normal operator action (the documented incremental address-publication path). An attacker-validator could also trigger it deliberately by being the first/only publisher.
new_findings.poc: .../scratchpad/verify-critic/node/poc_critic_peerdns_test.go::TestPoCCriticPartialPeerDNSPublicationHalts -> FAIL. publishers=[] (control) reaches height 76; publishers=[0,2] halts at height 3 (addresses confirmed committed on all nodes).
new_findings.fix: Fall back to the UNION of resolved addresses and the static/all-to-all peers while any current validator still lacks a published address (resolve peers only once EVERY current validator has an address), and make Neighbors over a key set that excludes self still connect self to that set. Document that addresses must be set for all validators in genesis, atomically, not rolled out incrementally.

new_findings.title: catchUp()/fastForward() do not re-run mempool.dropOverdrawn, so a node that self-recovers then proposes an overdrawing block that bans and destroys an honest payer's balance
locations: node/node.go:341-352 (fastForward changes balances but never prunes the mempool)
node/node.go:655-662 (commit DOES call dropOverdrawn, with a comment explaining exactly why skipping it bans the payer)
new_findings.description: commit() re-establishes the intake invariant after every block via mem.dropOverdrawn, because (its own comment) 'a pending overdraw left in the pool would make this node propose a block that bans — and destroys — the payer'. catchUp()/fastForward() change the committed balances the same way (adopting a peer's later state that may have debited a payer via payments admitted on other nodes, a reassignment, or a slash) but never run dropOverdrawn. A node that falls behind, self-recovers via the ordinary catch-up path, and is then the proposer will propose its still-pending payment set against the reduced balance; the ledger's overdraw ban fires on the honest payer, destroying its remaining balance and removing its account (and name). Every honest peer validates and commits that block.
new_findings.failure_scenario: Payer holds 100; node A admits payer->shop 60 (block 3) while payer has 100. Meanwhile the network commits height 2 carrying the payer's other 60-unit payment (handed to a different reference node); payer now holds 40. Node A catches up to height 3 via a verified checkpoint (the normal catchUpLoop path) WITHOUT pruning, is the height-3 proposer, and proposes the now-overdrawing 60; the payer is banned and its 40 destroyed — by an all-honest network. PoC confirms the proposed block is valid for every peer and leaves the payer at 0 / removed.
new_findings.attacker: None required (ordinary catch-up + payments split across reference nodes). An attacker could arrange the timing to grief a specific payer.
new_findings.poc: .../scratchpad/verify-critic/node/poc_critic_catchup_overdraw_test.go::TestPoCCriticCatchUpSkipsDropOverdrawn -> FAIL (after catchUp the node proposes X1; ApplyBlock valid==true, payer balance 0, account removed).
new_findings.fix: Call mem.dropOverdrawn (and updates/governance pruning as commit does) inside fastForward/catchUp after the new balances are set, before startHeight builds the candidate.

new_findings.title: Proposals are not bounded by maxRoundLookahead: one validator floods a single height with far-future-round proposals, growing node maps and making every later vote O(rounds)
locations: node/node.go:494-517 (onProposal accepts any round for which p.Proposer==driver.Proposer(round); no lookahead bound)
consensus/driver.go:216-218 (ReceiveVote DOES bound rounds to d.round+256 — the asymmetry)
consensus/driver.go:303-329 (step1 scans sortedPrecommitRounds and all prevote rounds every evaluate)
node/node.go:498-512,511 (each accepted proposal is stored in heightProposals and n.blocks and relayed)
new_findings.description: ReceiveVote rejects rounds beyond d.round+maxRoundLookahead (256), but onProposal/ReceiveProposal apply no such bound. ProposerAt is defined for every int32 round, and a single validator is the scheduled proposer for ~1/N of all rounds, so an attacker-validator can send authentic (correctly-signed, correct-proposer) proposals for ~2^31/N distinct rounds WITHIN one height. Each is stored in heightProposals and n.blocks (bodies up to ~1 MiB each over HTTP), relayed to peers (distinct relay keys, so no dedup), and allocates per-round VoteSets on first vote; every subsequent evaluate() pays an O(rounds) scan. These maps are reset at commit, but the height may not commit while under attack (and other validators are dragged along via relay).
new_findings.failure_scenario: 4 validators, one Byzantine. Hand-driven PoC: 20000 proposals for rounds >= 1000 (far beyond d.round+256) are all accepted, stored and marked for relay within height 1; n.blocks grows to 20001, live heap +23 MiB with a tiny 200-payment body, and one honest peer vote goes from 0.65ms to 21ms (O(rounds) evaluate). Scaling the body toward 1 MiB and the round count up exhausts memory / stalls the event loop network-wide via relay.
new_findings.attacker: A single validator (needs a validator key to be an authentic proposer; below 1/3).
new_findings.poc: .../scratchpad/verify-critic/node/poc_critic_rounds_test.go::TestPoCCriticProposalRoundsUnbounded -> FAIL (20000 far-future-round proposals accepted/stored/relayed; per-vote cost 0.65ms->21ms).
new_findings.fix: Apply the same maxRoundLookahead bound to onProposal/ReceiveProposal that ReceiveVote already uses (drop proposals with Round > d.round+256 or < 0), and cap heightProposals/n.blocks entries per height.

new_findings.title: The account-update pool admits fee-free, far-future updates from a key with no account and evicts only past blocks, so anyone reachable can fill it and block all honest registrations/re-delegations/address updates
locations: node/node.go:283-288 (evUpdate: admits any update that verifies its own signature and fits the message bound — no account/fee/BlockID-ceiling check)
node/updatepool.go:130-141 (add: bounded by maxMempool, content-dedup only)
node/httptransport.go:170-181 (handleAccountUpdate verifies only the self-signature, then SubmitUpdate)
new_findings.description: An AccountUpdate is admitted and gossiped if it carries a valid signature by its own From key and fits MaxMessageBytes. It need not correspond to any existing account, carries no fee, and has no BlockID upper bound; the pool (default maxMempool 10000) is pruned only for BlockID < height. A fresh keypair with no account on the ledger can sign maxMempool distinct updates naming a far-future block; they fill the pool, survive every commit, and from then on every honest update (name registration, re-delegation, the peer-DNS address publication of NEW-3) is refused at the full pool and never pools, gossips, or enacts. Mirrors the governance-pool-squat (C10) but on the update pool, which round 1 recorded as 'size-bounded and content-deduped' (sound) without noting the accountless/far-future/no-fee fill.
new_findings.failure_scenario: PoC with a 50-slot pool (stands for the 10000 default): a stranger key with NO account signs 50 updates naming block 2^40+i; across 9 commits they are never evicted and alice's valid name registration is refused (control with 0 squatters: alice's registration commits).
new_findings.attacker: Anyone who can reach the node's HTTP port (no account, no validator key) — the documented LAN trust boundary.
new_findings.fix: At update intake require From to be an existing account and bound BlockID to height+window; evict pooled updates for accounts that no longer exist or whose block window has passed. (Same root cause as C16's 'bound BlockID at intake' and C15's no-fee update fill — fixing those should cover this pool too.)

new_findings.title: saveSnapshot spawns one untracked backup goroutine per commit; on a hung BackupPath mount they accumulate one blocked OS thread per block until the process aborts
locations: node/persist.go:280-290 (go writeAtomic(...) per commit, deliberately untracked, may outlive Stop())
node/persist.go:297-319 (writeAtomic blocks in OpenFile/Write/Sync on the mount)
new_findings.description: When BackupPath is set, each commit launches a detached goroutine to mirror the checkpoint. If the backup target blocks (a stuck NFS/CIFS mount: open/write/fsync never return), the goroutine parks in a blocking syscall, which pins an OS thread AND holds a full copy of the checkpoint. There is no bound, no in-flight guard, and the goroutines are explicitly untracked, so they accumulate one per block. Go aborts the process once runtime threads hit 10000, so a long-enough stall on a mount the operator was told to use for durability crashes the validator. The operator guide does warn to prefer a local disk and that a failed mirror is 'silently ignored', which it is for errors — but a HANG is not an error and is not mentioned.
new_findings.failure_scenario: PoC: BackupPath points at a directory where the per-height temp path is a FIFO with no reader (models a hung mount). After ~150 commits the node has ~205 goroutines (was 2) and ~221 OS threads (was 6) — one per commit — while consensus keeps committing. Extrapolated, the process aborts at 10000 threads.
new_findings.attacker: None (operational: a backup mount that hangs rather than errors — exactly the NFS/CIFS case the docs steer away from but still support).
new_findings.fix: Serialise backup writes through a single worker with a depth-1 queue (drop/coalesce if the previous write is still in flight) and a write deadline/context, so a hung mount costs at most one blocked goroutine, not one per block.

new_findings.title: cmd/server load() discards the operator's peers list for a node whose key is not in validators when maxPeers>0, starting it with zero gossip peers
locations: cmd/server/config.go:196-216 (maxPeers>0 path replaces peers with Neighbors(validatorKeys, fc.PublicKey); Neighbors returns nil if self is not a validator key)
node/topology.go:84-87 (Neighbors returns nil when self not found in keys)
new_findings.description: With maxPeers>0 and a URL on every validator, load() replaces the configured peers with this node's Hypernode neighbours among the validator keys. If the node's own publicKey is not one of the validator entries (a non-validator reference/light node, or a simple key typo), Neighbors returns nil, so effective peers is empty: the node serves HTTP, admits payments and signs receipts, but relays to nobody and hears from nobody except via inbound POSTs. Silent — no error at load.
new_findings.failure_scenario: PoC: a node whose key is not in the 4-entry validators list, maxPeers=2, peers set to two real URLs -> load() returns effective peers = [] (the configured peers are discarded).
new_findings.fix: If Neighbors returns nil under maxPeers>0 (self not in the validator universe), fall back to the configured static peers rather than an empty list, or fail load() with a clear 'this node's publicKey is not among validators' error.
